summary: This document is a structured research discussion note (labeled L1, swarm_id L1) arguing that weekly/intermittent rapamycin does not universally spare mTORC2, as evidenced by tissue- and time-specific p-Akt S473 depression. It is not a primary experimental report but a hypothesis/claim document that synthesizes published literature and proposes a specific assay design to test the claim. It is relevant to TRL assessment as background scientific context for rapamycin-based longevity programs.

content_blocks.title: Claim and Core Hypothesis
content_blocks.content: Central claim: Intermittent or weekly rapamycin does NOT universally spare mTORC2. Specifically, at a pre-specified post-dose harvest in a pre-specified high-FKBP tissue or responder stratum, p-Akt S473 falls ≥25% versus vehicle even when group-mean skeletal muscle appears spared. This is framed as an 'assumption-kill' against the popular rationale that weekly/intermittent schedules are selectively mTORC1-biased and leave p-Akt S473 intact.

content_blocks.title: Why It Matters / Motivation
content_blocks.content: Popular trial rationale (including human trials) treats weekly/intermittent rapamycin as selectively mTORC1-biased, implying p-Akt S473 stays intact. Mouse group-mean muscle Westerns often appear spared vs. daily dosing, which is over-read as universal spare. Human weekly regimens (e.g., PEARL trial, PMID 40188830) lack published p-Akt S473 pharmacodynamic (PD) data, so the selectivity claim is unmeasured in the most clinically relevant context.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Chronic rapamycin disrupts mTORC2 and lowers p-Akt S473 (cell and in vivo). Intermittent schedules reduce the metabolic hit and often spare group-mean muscle p-Akt S473, but: (1) D3 sampling shows mean AKT ↓ ~29% (NS); (2) adipose can keep mTORC1 suppressed at D5; (3) FKBP12/FKBP51 ratio defines a tissue subset where mTORC2 inhibition still appears. Conclusion: mean muscle spare ≠ universal mTORC2 spare across time, tissue, or individuals.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claims vs. Measured Evidence
content_blocks.content:
Baseline claimed: Intermittent/weekly rapamycin preferentially inhibits mTORC1 and spares mTORC2, so p-Akt S473 remains intact between doses (unlike daily/chronic).

Baseline measured:
- Chronic exposure lowers p-Akt S473 and disrupts mTORC2 (PMID 16603397, 22461615).
- Weekly/intermittent mouse muscle group-mean p-Akt S473 often NS vs vehicle while daily hits.
- D3 weekly mean AKT ↓ ~29% NS.
- Tissue-subset hits via FKBP ratio (PMID 26463117, 25652038).
- Human weekly (PEARL) has no published p-Akt S473 PD (PMID 40188830) — UNKNOWN as human marker.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Sampling-time confound: D1 vs D3 vs D5/D7 harvest timing critically affects whether mTORC2 inhibition is detected.
2. Tissue/FKBP heterogeneity: mean muscle ≠ heart, adipose, islets, high-FKBP12 tissues.
3. Human weekly regimens lack p-Akt S473 (or equivalent mTORC2) PD panels.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
- PMID 26463117 / DOI 10.1111/acel.12405 (Arriola Apelo 2016): Intermittent vs daily; muscle p-Akt S473 often NS; D3 mean AKT ↓ ~29% NS.
- PMID 27091134 / DOI 10.1093/gerona/glw064: Intermittent lifespan efficacy ≠ universal mTORC2 spare.
- PMID 22461615 / DOI 10.1126/science.1215135: Chronic rapamycin impairs glucose metabolism via mTORC2 loss.
- PMID 25652038 / DOI 10.1111/acel.12313: mTORC2 (p-Akt S473) inhibition only in FKBP-ratio–defined tissue subset.
- PMID 40188830: PEARL trial — no published p-Akt S473 PD data for human weekly regimen.

content_blocks.content:

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design (Ablate / Refute Conditions)
content_blocks.content:
Ablation conditions (what must NOT be omitted for a valid test):
- Must specify harvest day (removing this → D1/D5-only can miss transient Akt depression).
- Must pre-specify tissue/FKBP stratum (mean muscle Western alone cannot kill universality).
- Must include responder-stratum contrast (NS group-mean is compatible with hidden depressed subset).

Refutation criterion: Under a pre-registered intermittent/weekly schedule, named tissue, and named harvest day, Western/ELISA p-Akt S473 shows <25% depression versus vehicle in EVERY pre-registered stratum (including FKBP-high tissues), while companion p-S6 remains suppressed.

Recommendation: Lock harvest day relative to last dose and one FKBP-high tissue (or blood mTORC2 PD proxy) before interpreting a null muscle Western as universal spare.

key_findings: Weekly/intermittent rapamycin does not universally spare mTORC2: p-Akt S473 can fall ≥25% vs vehicle in pre-specified high-FKBP tissues or responder strata even when group-mean skeletal muscle appears spared.
D3 post-dose sampling in weekly rapamycin mouse studies shows mean AKT ↓ ~29% (NS) in muscle (PMID 26463117), indicating transient mTORC2 suppression that is missed by D1 or D7 sampling.
FKBP12/FKBP51 ratio defines a tissue subset where mTORC2 inhibition (p-Akt S473 depression) still occurs under intermittent rapamycin (PMID 25652038).
Chronic rapamycin impairs glucose metabolism via mTORC2 loss (PMID 22461615, 16603397), establishing the mechanistic basis for concern.
Human weekly rapamycin trials (PEARL, PMID 40188830) have no published p-Akt S473 pharmacodynamic data — the mTORC2-sparing claim is unmeasured in humans.
The proposed assay requires: pre-specified harvest day, pre-specified FKBP-high tissue, responder-stratum contrast, Western/ELISA p-Akt S473 with companion p-S6, and ≥25% depression threshold.
Adipose tissue can maintain mTORC1 suppression at D5 post-dose, indicating tissue-specific and time-specific pharmacodynamics that differ from skeletal muscle.
This document is a research discussion/hypothesis note (TRL 1 level), not a primary experimental report; no new experimental data are generated.
